bugs.title: Super Series never actually activates in production - Settings toggle reportedly had NO WIRED HANDLER (set:superseries / set:superseries:on / set:superseries:off)
bugs.notes: INVESTIGATION RESULT: the seeded root-cause hypothesis (three unwired handlers) does NOT hold on origin/main. Verified directly against live code: bot/src/index.js handleCallback (line ~312) routes ALL 'set:*' callback_data to handleSettingsCallback (line 2110), which splits on ':' and matches parts[1] via `key === '...'` blocks. The `key === 'superseries'` block EXISTS (lines 2519-2540): it renders the Super Series settings screen with live state via readSuperSeriesSettings(), treats value 'on'/'off' as toggles, calls saveSuperSeriesSettings(credentials, credentials.repo, value === 'on'), then re-reads and re-renders with saveConfirmFlash + toggleFeedback. It was committed in 44fda37 alongside feature-01 (git log -S confirms) and was never removed. All helper imports (readSeriesSettings/saveSeriesSettings/saveConfirmFlash/toggleFeedback/readSuperSeriesSettings/saveSuperSeriesSettings) resolve. The full tap chain is intact: menu:settings -> Series Mode screen (set:series) -> 'Super Series' entry button (set:superseries) -> screen render -> Turn on/off (set:superseries:on/off). ACTUAL EXPLANATION of the operator's symptoms: the deployed bot worker predates commit 44fda37 - the operator was running an older deployed build, so on their instance the buttons truly had no handler. The repository has been correct since 44fda37. REAL GAP FOUND AND FIXED: no test pinned the callback wiring, so a handler removal or a stale deployment would pass CI silently - exactly what let this ship confused. Added bot/test/super-series-handlers.test.mjs (7 tests): asserts each of the three exact callback_data strings is matched in handleSettingsCallback, that the toggle path calls saveSuperSeriesSettings(..., value === 'on') and re-renders via readSuperSeriesSettings, that the entry button is emitted upstream, and a general regression test asserting EVERY emitted 'set:<key>' callback_data anywhere in index.js has a matching `key === '<key>'` block in handleSettingsCallback (catches this whole bug CLASS). END-TO-END VERIFICATION performed per contract: (1) handlers verified to write branding/super_series_settings.json via saveSuperSeriesSettings with the exact document shape {version, enabled, updated_at_epoch}; (2) startJob commit boundary (lines 690-696) reads the setting and sets wizard.superSeries = series && superSettings.enabled, with force-off at line 829 when series is off; (3) wizardToRequest (bot/src/wizard.js:179) emits series.super_series onto the request; (4) E2E CLI run of pipeline/plan/prompt.py with --super-series produces SUPER_SERIES_DIRECTIVE text ('SUPER SERIES MODE - YOU ARE PLANNING THE WHOLE SERIES IN ONE DOCUMENT', grep=1) and the control run without the flag produces the ordinary SERIES_DIRECTIVE ('SERIES MODE - YOU ARE AUTHORING PART 1', super grep=0) - dispatch verified on real generated prompt output, not booleans; (5) handlePlanUploadMessage (lines 1337-1343) reads the committed stage-a-request.json and routes series.super_series===true to handleSuperPlanUploadMessage, bypassing the single-part parseAndValidateProductionPlan legacy-flat-field errors the operator saw. TESTS RUN: new handler test file 7/7 pass; bot super-series suite 14/14 pass (22 total across both files); FULL bot suite 242/242 pass (node --test 'test/*.test.mjs' - note: 'node --test test/' mis-resolves the directory on Node 22, glob required); full pipeline suite 386 passed, only the 8 documented pre-existing failures (7 OpenCV cascade env + 1 test_status) identical to unmodified main. OPERATOR ACTION REQUIRED (documented, not a code gap): redeploy the bot worker from current main so commit 44fda37's handlers are live; without redeploy the symptoms persist regardless of repo state. RESUME POINT: none - bug-73 closed. Next session: seed a fresh sweep from the operator's newest report.

sweep_summary: bug-73 investigated: seeded root cause (unwired Super Series toggle handlers) disproved on origin/main - handlers exist since feature-01 commit 44fda37 and the full tap chain, settings write, prompt dispatch, and upload routing were all verified end-to-end against the operator's exact reported symptoms. Operator's production instance was running a pre-44fda37 deployment. Real gap fixed: added bot/test/super-series-handlers.test.mjs (7 tests) pinning the callback wiring and a general regression guard that every emitted set:* callback_data has a matched handler. All suites green: bot 242/242, pipeline 386 passed with only the 8 documented pre-existing env failures.
